beats.heading: Agents author, people read
beats.body: An agent states meaning through the CLI. The Archboard server checks the write, takes the board's lease, commits the whole family to disk and only then answers. Nothing else writes a board.

beats.heading: The browser is a viewer

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Authors named boards: one short-lived process per command, run by the source of the archboard checkout it stands in, writing no board itself
nodes.description: Every board operation reaches the Archboard server over HTTP and names the vault the command found, from -C or the checkout it runs in. nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: Serves the Archboard browser and CLI. Each Archboard checkout runs its own server on its own port.
nodes.description: One process for each archboard checkout, running that checkout's source: the main checkout's listens on port 3000, a linked worktree's on a port from 10000 to 19999 that its path decides. nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads architecture; owns the camera, the view, the walkthrough and the selection, and nothing else
nodes.description: It also carries voice: the Archboard server negotiates the session with Codex for the page, and the microphone and the voice then travel over the connection that negotiation opens.

nodes.name: Board vault
nodes.responsibility: One document per board, holding every variant of it
nodes.description: Tracked in the repository. The file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it: an accepted write is on disk, fsync included, before it is answered (ADR 0015, ADR 0023).

nodes.name: Codex app-server
nodes.responsibility: Runs each host's tab sessions as one private child over stdio.
nodes.description: Its own process group, spoken to over stdio; what it keeps is in the Codex home. Its threads author boards the way any agent does, by running the CLI from a sandbox that reaches the server over localhost. The child's environment names the URL of the server that started it and no vault, so that CLI talks to that server and never starts another. A thread finds each board's vault in its board context and names it with -C. Archboard's side of it is the agent workbench inside the Archboard server.

nodes.name: Repository checkout
nodes.responsibility: Every checkout known here, the one chosen for each repository that bindings resolve in, and untracked vaults; each checkout holds its configured language servers
nodes.description: A binding names a repository identity and a path inside it, which are the same in every clone; a machine-local registry is the only place a directory on one machine is written down. It holds every known checkout (clones, and the worktrees of its identity that git lists for a known one), each with its identity, and every registered directory outside a checkout that holds .archboard/vault, under a registry name. For each identity one checkout is chosen: the first known one, then only repo use changes it, and repo add never does. A reader that turns an identity into a directory asks code-target, which reads the chosen checkouts and so never sees the others, with one exception: a binding that names the identity of the checkout that holds the vault being read resolves in that checkout, registered or chosen or not (ADR 0049). An identity whose chosen checkout was forgotten resolves as unregistered, unless the vault stands in it. Each checkout's entry also holds the language servers an agent set with repo language-server (TASK-433): a command and its arguments for Python, C (which covers C++ and Objective-C), C# or Swift, kept with the checkout and removed with it.
